Philippine Peso Holds at Record Low Amid Rising Oil Prices

The Philippine peso has held steady at its record low, despite rising oil prices and concerns about the central bank's ability to defend it. The central bank maintains it doesn't aim to defend a specific level. Bloomberg reported that rising crude and US rate-hike bets may push the rupee to an even lower level. The peso has been declining against the US dollar due to higher oil prices, which have increased by 10% in the past month. The Philippine government has announced plans to increase fuel subsidies to cushion the impact on consumers. The central bank's decision not to intervene in the foreign exchange market has raised concerns about the stability of the currency.
